pubcol-w-53bd7d992ed7edf9.definition_en: to reach out and hold something, or to carry, accept, or need something
pubcol-w-53bd7d992ed7edf9.example_simple: Please take a seat while you wait for the doctor.
pubcol-w-53bd7d992ed7edf9.example_complex: It will take considerable patience and time to master a foreign language properly.

pubcol-w-e368e2ce8ce09537.definition_en: to go on a journey or excursion by boat, usually for pleasure
collocations: take a boat trip along the river
take a boat trip around the island
pubcol-w-e368e2ce8ce09537.example_simple: We took a boat trip along the coast last summer.
pubcol-w-e368e2ce8ce09537.example_complex: During our holiday in Ha Long Bay, we took a boat trip that wound between hundreds of limestone islands.

pubcol-w-7afc62b8cbf82df1.definition_en: to stop working or an activity for a short time in order to rest
pubcol-w-7afc62b8cbf82df1.example_simple: Let's take a break and have some coffee.
pubcol-w-7afc62b8cbf82df1.example_complex: After hours of intense revision, she decided to take a break and go for a walk to clear her head.

pubcol-w-759d9e6a6de655ec.definition_en: to study for and obtain an academic qualification at a university
collocations: take a degree at a top university
pubcol-w-759d9e6a6de655ec.example_simple: She took a degree at the university in London.
pubcol-w-759d9e6a6de655ec.example_complex: He took a degree at the university in mechanical engineering before pursuing a career in aerospace design.

pubcol-w-8dc3a5a756a62157.definition_en: to begin to like someone or something, often suddenly
collocations: take a fancy to an idea
pubcol-w-8dc3a5a756a62157.example_simple: My little sister took a fancy to the stray cat next door.
pubcol-w-8dc3a5a756a62157.example_complex: He had never shown interest in gardening, but on retirement he took a fancy to growing orchids.

pubcol-w-74349788b0e51a3d.definition_en: to make a photographic image of a person
collocations: take a photograph of the group
take a photograph of the bride
take a clear photograph of someone
pubcol-w-74349788b0e51a3d.example_simple: Can you take a photograph of me in front of the temple?
pubcol-w-74349788b0e51a3d.example_complex: The journalist asked permission before taking a photograph of the elderly craftsman at his workbench.

pubcol-w-c40ac18ec2b94073.definition_en: to feel sympathy for someone and help them because of it
collocations: take pity on a stray animal
take pity on someone in trouble
pubcol-w-c40ac18ec2b94073.example_simple: She took pity on the hungry dog and gave it some food.
pubcol-w-c40ac18ec2b94073.example_complex: The examiner took pity on the nervous candidate and repeated the question more slowly.
pubcol-w-c40ac18ec2b94073.vi_meaning_correction: thương hại, thông cảm và giúp đỡ ai

pubcol-w-627641fad3cec951.definition_en: to politely refuse an offer now while suggesting you may accept it later
collocations: take a rain check on dinner
can I take a rain check
take a rain check for now
pubcol-w-627641fad3cec951.example_simple: I'm too tired tonight, so can I take a rain check on the movie?
pubcol-w-627641fad3cec951.example_complex: Grateful for the invitation but overwhelmed with work, she asked to take a rain check until the following month.

pubcol-w-217b6af1776a407e.definition_en: to adopt a particular opinion or way of thinking about something
pubcol-w-217b6af1776a407e.example_simple: The teacher takes a strict view of students who arrive late.
pubcol-w-217b6af1776a407e.example_complex: Economists take differing views on whether raising interest rates will curb inflation without stalling growth.

pubcol-w-7b810d262268c2f5.definition_en: to spend a year away from study or work, often before starting university
collocations: take a year out to travel
take a year out before university
take a year out to work
pubcol-w-7b810d262268c2f5.example_simple: He decided to take a year out to travel before going to college.
pubcol-w-7b810d262268c2f5.example_complex: Many students take a year out to gain work experience, believing it makes them more mature when they finally start their degree.
pubcol-w-7b810d262268c2f5.vi_meaning_correction: dành ra một năm nghỉ (thường trước khi vào đại học)

pubcol-w-1e5ec003b4a45e09.definition_en: to do something in order to deal with a problem or situation
pubcol-w-1e5ec003b4a45e09.example_simple: The government must take action to reduce pollution.
pubcol-w-1e5ec003b4a45e09.example_complex: Unless companies take urgent action to cut emissions, the environmental damage may soon become irreversible.

pubcol-w-a742d8cb8f93aa4b.definition_en: to carry out measures or steps to achieve something or solve a problem
pubcol-w-a742d8cb8f93aa4b.example_simple: We need to take actions to protect the environment.
pubcol-w-a742d8cb8f93aa4b.example_complex: The committee agreed to take a series of coordinated actions aimed at improving workplace safety.
pubcol-w-a742d8cb8f93aa4b.vi_meaning_correction: thực hiện các hành động, thi hành các biện pháp

pubcol-w-de15b27eb22d82fd.definition_en: to make good use of an opportunity, or to unfairly exploit someone
pubcol-w-de15b27eb22d82fd.example_simple: You should take advantage of the free lessons while you can.
pubcol-w-de15b27eb22d82fd.example_complex: Savvy investors took advantage of the market downturn to buy shares at greatly reduced prices.

pubcol-w-eadfdf122da6be50.definition_en: to side firmly with someone and support their position
pubcol-w-eadfdf122da6be50.example_simple: In the argument, he took colour with his old friend.
pubcol-w-eadfdf122da6be50.example_complex: During the dispute over the merger, several board members quietly took colour with the chairman despite public doubts.

pubcol-w-f77779de050ec6cf.definition_en: to get great pleasure or enjoyment from something
pubcol-w-f77779de050ec6cf.example_simple: The children take delight in playing in the snow.
pubcol-w-f77779de050ec6cf.example_complex: She took obvious delight in surprising her guests with dishes they had never tasted before.

pubcol-w-8158cf877d873618.definition_en: to take extreme or severe steps to deal with a serious problem
collocations: take drastic measures to cut costs
pubcol-w-8158cf877d873618.example_simple: The company had to take drastic measures to avoid going bankrupt.
pubcol-w-8158cf877d873618.example_complex: Faced with a collapsing water supply, the city took drastic measures, rationing usage and banning all non-essential consumption.
pubcol-w-8158cf877d873618.vi_meaning_correction: áp dụng những biện pháp quyết liệt, mạnh tay

pubcol-w-9c681609bfb9f689.definition_en: to begin to produce results, or (of a law or rule) to come into force
pubcol-w-9c681609bfb9f689.example_simple: The painkiller took effect after about twenty minutes.
pubcol-w-9c681609bfb9f689.example_complex: The new tax regulations take effect at the start of the financial year, giving businesses little time to adjust.

pubcol-w-3ab3368d16b5e5b5.definition_en: to object strongly to something or feel offended by it
pubcol-w-3ab3368d16b5e5b5.example_simple: She took exception to his rude comment about her work.
pubcol-w-3ab3368d16b5e5b5.example_complex: The senator took exception to the implication that his vote had been influenced by donations.
pubcol-w-3ab3368d16b5e5b5.vi_meaning_correction: phản đối, bất bình với điều gì

pubcol-w-e9b54dabe37b5422.definition_en: to consider something when making a decision or judgement
pubcol-w-e9b54dabe37b5422.example_simple: You should take into account the weather before planning the trip.
pubcol-w-e9b54dabe37b5422.example_complex: When assessing the essays, examiners take into account not only grammar but also coherence and range of vocabulary.

pubcol-w-d1f86d00872cba12.definition_en: to think carefully about something before reaching a decision
pubcol-w-d1f86d00872cba12.example_simple: The judge took into consideration his difficult childhood.
pubcol-w-d1f86d00872cba12.example_complex: Taking into consideration the tight budget and the short timeline, the team opted for a simpler design.

pubcol-w-23e524e47a16798f.definition_en: to assume something is true or certain without questioning it, or to fail to appreciate someone
pubcol-w-23e524e47a16798f.example_simple: We often take clean water for granted until there is a shortage.
pubcol-w-23e524e47a16798f.example_complex: Having grown up in a wealthy family, he took for granted comforts that most people could only dream of.
pubcol-w-23e524e47a16798f.vi_meaning_correction: coi là điều hiển nhiên; không biết trân trọng

pubcol-w-7c2786393bacb3ec.definition_en: to rent a piece of land for a fixed period under a legal agreement
collocations: take land on a long lease
take land on lease from the council
pubcol-w-7c2786393bacb3ec.example_simple: The farmer took some land on lease to grow more crops.
pubcol-w-7c2786393bacb3ec.example_complex: Unable to afford the purchase price, the young entrepreneur took the land on lease for ten years to build his warehouse.

pubcol-w-7678dccc6843a29c.definition_en: to take official or planned steps in order to achieve or prevent something
pubcol-w-7678dccc6843a29c.example_simple: The school took measures to keep the students safe.
pubcol-w-7678dccc6843a29c.example_complex: Authorities took sweeping measures to contain the outbreak, closing schools and restricting travel between provinces.
